title: Finite-valued Cech cocycles descend with their equation to a finite quotient surjection
statement:
Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $q:T\to S$ be a continuous surjection of compact Hausdorff totally disconnected spaces, and let $M$ be a finite abelian group with the discrete topology. For $r\geq1$ write $T_S^r=\{(t_0,\ldots,t_{r-1})\in T^r:q(t_0)=\cdots=q(t_{r-1})\}$ with its subspace topology. Fix an integer $n\geq1$ and a continuous map $c:T_S^{n+1}\to M$ such that
$$\sum_{j=0}^{n+1}(-1)^j c(t_0,\ldots,\widehat{t_j},\ldots,t_{n+1})=0\quad\text{for every }(t_0,\ldots,t_{n+1})\in T_S^{n+2}.$$
There exist finite discrete sets $T_0,S_0$, continuous surjections $a:T\to T_0$, $b:S\to S_0$, a surjection $q_0:T_0\to S_0$ with $q_0a=bq$, and a function $c_0:(T_0)_{S_0}^{n+1}\to M$ such that
$$c(t_0,\ldots,t_n)=c_0(a(t_0),\ldots,a(t_n))$$
for every tuple in $T_S^{n+1}$, and
$$\sum_{j=0}^{n+1}(-1)^j c_0(x_0,\ldots,\widehat{x_j},\ldots,x_{n+1})=0\quad\text{for every }(x_0,\ldots,x_{n+1})\in(T_0)_{S_0}^{n+2}.$$
Here $(T_0)_{S_0}^r$ denotes the tuples with equal $q_0$-images. Empty spaces and the zero coefficient group are included. No surjectivity of $T_S^r\to(T_0)_{S_0}^r$ is asserted.

source.place: Tags 08ZY (lemma-profinite), 08ZZ (lemma-profinite-refine-open-covering), and 0A2P (lemma-describe-limits), applied to compatible finite quotient diagrams. Agent-formulated finite Cech cocycle descent, supplying the discrete-coefficient input implicit in Bhatt–Scholze, The pro-etale topology for schemes, Lemma 4.3.9(2), PDF printed page 33; not a verbatim standalone assertion of those tags.

proof.text: If $S=\varnothing$, the map $q$ forces $T=\varnothing$. Take $T_0=S_0=\varnothing$ and the unique maps and function. All assertions are vacuous since every tuple length is positive. Henceforth $S$ and $T$ are nonempty. Put $k=n+1$. Repeated application of [lem-sfb-finite-quotient-fiber-product] gives compact Hausdorff totally disconnected spaces $T^r$ and $P_r=T_S^r$ for every $r\geq1$: use the base point to form ordinary products, and use $P_{r+1}=P_r\times_S T$ for the fibre powers, starting with $P_1=T$. The identifications with tuple subspaces and the maps to $S$ are given by the coordinates. In particular $P_k$ is compact and coordinate-deletion maps are continuous.

source.place: Tags 08ZY (lemma-profinite) and 08ZZ (lemma-profinite-refine-open-covering), finite clopen partition construction; agent-written application to the given cocycle.

proof.text: For each $z\in P_k$, continuity of $c$ into discrete $M$ gives an open neighbourhood $O_z$ of $z$ in $T^k$ such that $c=c(z)$ on $O_z\cap P_k$. By the finite-product topology choose a rectangle around $z$ inside $O_z$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-clopen-basis] in $T$ to each coordinate neighbourhood to obtain a clopen rectangle $R_z=\prod_{i=0}^{k-1}U_{z,i}$ around $z$ with $R_z\subseteq O_z$. Compactness of $P_k$ selects finitely many $R_1,\ldots,R_N$ covering it; $c$ is constant on each $R_l\cap P_k$.

source.place: Tags 08ZY (lemma-profinite) and 08ZZ (lemma-profinite-refine-open-covering), finite clopen partition construction; agent-written application to the given cocycle.

proof.text: Let $\alpha$ consist of the nonempty atoms of the finite family of clopens $U_{l,i}$ in $T$: an atom is an intersection choosing each $U_{l,i}$ or its complement. Thus $\alpha$ is a finite partition into nonempty clopens. For any $k$-tuple of its blocks $A_0,\ldots,A_{k-1}$ whose product meets $P_k$, choose a point $z$ of that intersection and an $R_l$ containing $z$. Membership in every $U_{l,i}$ is constant on $A_i$, so $\prod_iA_i\subseteq R_l$. Consequently $c$ is constant on $(\prod_iA_i)\cap P_k$. Define $h:T^k\to M$ to have this constant value on $\prod_iA_i$ if the intersection is nonempty, and value $0$ otherwise. This is well-defined, agrees with $c$ on $P_k$, and is continuous: each fibre is a union of the finitely many clopen product cells.

source.place: Tags 08ZY (lemma-profinite) and 08ZZ (lemma-profinite-refine-open-covering), finite clopen partition construction; agent-written application to the given cocycle.

proof.text:
Define the continuous function $e:T^{k+1}\to M$ by
$$e(t_0,\ldots,t_k)=\sum_{j=0}^k(-1)^j h(t_0,\ldots,\widehat{t_j},\ldots,t_k).$$
Continuity follows because coordinate deletions are continuous and finite sums in discrete $M$ are continuous. Its nonzero locus $D=e^{-1}(M\setminus\{0\})$ is clopen, hence compact as a closed subset of compact $T^{k+1}$. Every face of a tuple in $P_{k+1}$ belongs to $P_k$, where $h=c$; the assumed equation therefore gives $e|_{P_{k+1}}=0$. Thus for each $t\in D$ there are indices $i,j$ with $q(t_i)\ne q(t_j)$.

source.place: Tags 08ZY (lemma-profinite) and 08ZZ (lemma-profinite-refine-open-covering), finite clopen partition construction; agent-written application to the given cocycle.

proof.text:
For each $t\in D$ choose such $i,j$. Hausdorffness makes $S\setminus\{q(t_j)\}$ an open neighbourhood of $q(t_i)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-clopen-basis] in $S$ to choose a clopen $V_t$ containing $q(t_i)$ and excluding $q(t_j)$. The open set
$$W_t=\{u\in T^{k+1}:q(u_i)\in V_t,\ q(u_j)\notin V_t\}$$
contains $t$. Compactness of $D$ selects finitely many $W_t$ covering $D$. Let $\gamma$ be the partition of $S$ into the nonempty atoms of their finitely many clopens $V_t$ (the partition $\{S\}$ when the family is empty). A tuple $u$ whose $q(u_i)$ all lie in the same $\gamma$-block belongs to none of these $W_t$: membership in each selected $V_t$ is constant on a block. Hence such a tuple lies outside $D$, and $e(u)=0$.

source.place: Tags 08ZY (lemma-profinite) and 08ZZ (lemma-profinite-refine-open-covering), finite clopen partition construction; agent-written application to the given cocycle.

proof.text:
Refine $\alpha$ to the finite clopen partition
$$\beta=\{A\cap q^{-1}(B): A\in\alpha,\ B\in\gamma,\ A\cap q^{-1}(B)\ne\varnothing\}.$$
Let $T_0=\beta$, $S_0=\gamma$, and let $a,b$ send a point to its block. The maps are continuous surjections because the blocks are open and nonempty. Define $q_0(C)=B$ for the unique $B\in\gamma$ with $C\subseteq q^{-1}(B)$. This is well-defined and $q_0a=bq$. Given $B\in\gamma$, choose $s\in B$ and then $t$ with $q(t)=s$; its $\beta$-block maps to $B$. Thus $q_0$ is surjective.

source.place: Tags 08ZY (lemma-profinite) and 08ZZ (lemma-profinite-refine-open-covering), finite clopen partition construction; agent-written application to the given cocycle.

proof.text:
Because $\beta$ refines $\alpha$, the function $h$ is constant on each product of $k$ blocks of $\beta$. Write $h_0:T_0^k\to M$ for the corresponding function and restrict it to $c_0:(T_0)_{S_0}^k\to M$. For $(t_0,\ldots,t_{k-1})\in P_k$, compatibility $q_0a=bq$ places its block tuple in this domain, and
$$c_0(a(t_0),\ldots,a(t_{k-1}))=h(t_0,\ldots,t_{k-1})=c(t_0,\ldots,t_{k-1}).$$

source.place: Tags 08ZY (lemma-profinite) and 08ZZ (lemma-profinite-refine-open-covering), finite clopen partition construction; agent-written application to the given cocycle.

proof.text:
For any $(x_0,\ldots,x_k)\in(T_0)_{S_0}^{k+1}$, independently choose representatives $t_i\in x_i$. Their $q$-images lie in the single $\gamma$-block $q_0(x_i)$, so step 5 gives $e(t_0,\ldots,t_k)=0$. Each face of the block tuple belongs to $(T_0)_{S_0}^k$ and the definition of $h_0$ gives
$$\sum_{j=0}^k(-1)^j c_0(x_0,\ldots,\widehat{x_j},\ldots,x_k)=\sum_{j=0}^k(-1)^j h(t_0,\ldots,\widehat{t_j},\ldots,t_k)=e(t_0,\ldots,t_k)=0.$$
The representatives need not have equal $q$-images. This verifies the equation even on block tuples with no lift to $P_{k+1}$. When $M$ is the zero group, $h=e=0$, $D=\varnothing$, and the same construction applies.

The resulting compatible finite partitions preserve the cocycle equation even on nonliftable tuples. Reused two existing nodes; no new nodes.
